study: Exploratory second policy round after reviewing the incremental predictive ranks and the fixed-width guarded policy. No new untouched cohorts. Lock model, utility and candidate pool before running this cross-width rule.
cohorts: All 41 prior PMLB budgeted-guard folds, equal task weight; the previously opened Optdigits holdout is a separate retrospective sensitivity. Do not tune using these scores.
primary: Use estimates trained on the uniform-deletion cohort in incremental_prediction on the OTHER 13 tasks. Use path-trained models as secondary. On Optdigits take the arithmetic mean of the 14 saved independent-task model probabilities (no Optdigits data used for model coefficients).
nomination: Choose one candidate from the union across all widths of the same deterministic budgeted_guard pool to maximize d*(1-p_hat) where d=1-|S|/|A|. Compare p_hat from identical training designs using size alone or size plus the minimum four-panel masked approval count. Take highest utility then smallest sum of Gain ranks then smallest column IDs. If pool empty, use A. Fallback to A if the single freshly fitted candidate fails the same disjoint guard. Only one candidate guard refit plus its anchor for both methods.
outcome: Same actual utility d if the final refitted support passes the observed outer tolerance and zero otherwise, paired fold-specific AUC, accuracy, realized breach, retention and differences. Report changes in proposed widths and identities, observed guard acceptance, fold losses and wins, per-task bootstrap on 14 task contrasts (30000, seed 33119), all results for both source models. Measured component cost recharges common candidate preparation and full all-width voting for the augmented rule. Exclude historical training and audit I/O, describe as marginal application with pretrained meta-models.
